shape.description: Same legs, arches and body as B-01. The top is a broad curved channel, a quarter of a ring centred on the inner corner (SW here), that carries the marble in at the W face and turns it 90 degrees out of the S face. Both those faces show a U notch with a tab loop under it. The outer (NE) half of the top is a flat high rim. The inner corner is a leg ridge that rises up the corner to a small peg. The pointed back corner in VTech's drawing is the flat rim corner seen in iso view, not a spike.
shape.sizeBasis: Scaled from the floor cell (about 45 mm, one block width) against VTech parts drawings and Joey's photos; +-10%. No ruler in any photo.

assumptions: Axes: +x = E, +y = S, z up; z is in slots above this block's own feet. Marble seat in a cup is z=0.68.

Joint rule: a block body is about a cube; pitch is 1 slot; rails stand 0.17 slot higher and nest inside the block above. Each face has a low arch, as tall as the cup is deep (0.33 slot). So the arch of an upper block plus the cup end of the lower block make a round hole at the joint, about 0.65 slot across. The cup-end port and the side round hole are the SAME port: it is a notch when the stack ends there and a hole when a block sits on top. Height is the same either way, n-0.32 slots for the nth block.
Turn is left or right by rotation only; there is no mirrored part. Which way a marble enters is free.
